## Solution

We analyze the convergence of

$$I(p) = \int_0^\infty \frac{\log x}{1+x^p}\,dx$$

by examining the two endpoints $x \to 0^+$ and $x \to +\infty$ separately.

---

### Behavior near $x = 0^+$

**Case $p > 0$:** As $x \to 0^+$, $x^p \to 0$, so $1+x^p \to 1$ and the integrand satisfies $\frac{\log x}{1+x^p} \sim \log x$. Since

$$\int_0^\varepsilon \log x\,dx = \big[x\log x - x\big]_0^\varepsilon \to -\varepsilon \quad (\text{finite}),$$

the integral converges near $0$ for every $p > 0$.

**Case $p = 0$:** $1+x^0 = 2$, integrand $= \frac{1}{2}\log x$, which diverges at $+\infty$ (treated below).

**Case $p < 0$:** Writing $q = -p > 0$, as $x\to 0^+$ we have $x^p = x^{-q}\to\infty$, so $1+x^p \sim x^{-q}$ and the integrand $\sim \log x \cdot x^{q}$. Then

$$\int_0^\varepsilon x^{q}\log x\,dx$$

converges for $q > -1$, i.e. $-p>-1$, i.e. $p<1$. Since $p<0<1$, this **always converges** near $0$.

---

### Behavior near $x = +\infty$

**Case $p > 0$:** As $x\to\infty$, $x^p\to\infty$, so $1+x^p\sim x^p$ and the integrand $\sim \frac{\log x}{x^p}$. The integral

$$\int_M^\infty \frac{\log x}{x^p}\,dx$$

converges if and only if $p > 1$ (since $\log x = o(x^\varepsilon)$ for any $\varepsilon>0$, comparison with $\int x^{-(p-\varepsilon)}dx$ shows convergence exactly when $p>1$). At the boundary $p=1$:

$$\int_M^\infty \frac{\log x}{x}\,dx = \tfrac12(\log x)^2\Big|_M^\infty = +\infty,$$

so $p=1$ diverges.

**Case $p = 0$:** Integrand $=\frac12\log x$, and $\int^\infty \log x\,dx = +\infty$. Diverges.

**Case $p < 0$:** As $x\to\infty$, $x^p\to 0$, so $1+x^p\to 1$ and the integrand $\sim \log x$. Since $\int^\infty \log x\,dx = +\infty$, the integral **diverges**.

---

### Combining both endpoints

| Range of $p$ | Near $0$ | Near $\infty$ | Overall |
|---|---|---|---|
| $p > 1$ | converges | converges | **converges** |
| $p = 1$ | converges | diverges | diverges |
| $0 < p < 1$ | converges | diverges | diverges |
| $p = 0$ | converges | diverges | diverges |
| $p < 0$ | converges | diverges | diverges |

The integral converges at both endpoints **if and only if $p > 1$**.

---

**Conclusion.** The integral $\displaystyle\int_0^\infty \frac{\log x}{1+x^p}\,dx$ converges if and only if

$$\boxed{p > 1}.$$
